title: There will be another winter
literal_meaning: Cold does not finish with a single Magha.
explanation: One difficult season is not the last occasion on which we may need help. The saying can warn against treating a temporary advantage as permanent, or remind someone who refuses help that circumstances may change. Tone matters: it can sound like practical advice or a pointed warning.
meaning_odia: ମାଘର ଶୀତ ଥରକରେ ସରେନାହିଁ; ପୁଣି ସେମିତି ଦିନ ଆସିପାରେ—ଏହି ଭାବରେ କଥାଟି କୁହାଯାଏ। ଆଜି ଯାହାର ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ, କାଲି ତାହାର ଦରକାର ପଡ଼ିପାରେ। ଏଥିରେ ଆଗାମୀ ଦିନ ଓ ପରସ୍ପରର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ମନେ ପକାଇବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅଛି, ପାଗର ପୂର୍ବାନୁମାନ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: After borrowing a tool successfully once, someone dismisses the neighbour who lent it. Another person reminds them that they may need that neighbour again. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Magha supplies the seasonal image. The central point is recurring need and changing fortunes, not a precise forecast or a claim that cold is confined to one calendar month.

title: From scarcity into famine
literal_meaning: To go from high prices into famine.
explanation: A change meant to escape difficulty leads into something worse. Here କାନ୍ତାର is the dictionary’s famine sense, not its separate forest sense.
meaning_odia: ଦରବୃଦ୍ଧିର ଅସୁବିଧାରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିବାକୁ ଯାଇ ଦୁର୍ଭିକ୍ଷ ପରି ଆହୁରି ବଡ଼ କଷ୍ଟରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଉତ୍ସର ଏହି ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ‘କାନ୍ତାର’ର ଅର୍ଥ ଦୁର୍ଭିକ୍ଷ, ବଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ଅସୁବିଧା ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ବାଟ ବାଛିବା ବେଳେ ନୂଆ ବାଟର ବିପଦ ବି ଦେଖିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
usage_example: A shop changes to a cheaper supplier, then loses more because deliveries repeatedly fail. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The food-scarcity image supplies the comparison; no particular famine or historical event is identified.

title: Kartika brings a chill at night
explanation: The echo between କାର୍ତ୍ତିକି and ରାତିକି makes a seasonal observation easy to remember. The line draws attention to night rather than declaring that the whole day has turned cold. In conversation it can accompany noticing a change in the air. This is a calendar-linked saying, not a forecast for every place or year.
meaning_odia: କାର୍ତ୍ତିକି ସହ ରାତିକିର ମିଳ ଋତୁର କଥାକୁ ମନରେ ରଖିଦିଏ। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଦିନସାରା ଶୀତର କଥା ନକହି ରାତିର ଥଣ୍ଡାକୁ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରେ। ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟା ପରେ ପବନ ବଦଳିଥିବା ଅନୁଭବ କଲେ ଏହି କଥା ମନେ ପଡ଼ିପାରେ। ସବୁ ଜାଗାରେ ସବୁ ବର୍ଷ ଏକା ପାଗ ହେବ ବୋଲି ଏହାକୁ ଧରିବା ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: A rhyme links Kartika with the chill felt at night.
odia_summary: କାର୍ତ୍ତିକ ଓ ରାତିର ଶୀତକୁ ଶବ୍ଦର ମିଳ ମନେ ରଖାଏ।
usage_example: While sitting outside after sunset in Kartika, someone reaches for a shawl and repeats the line. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
cultural_context: Source identifies Kartiki with Kartika and labels the line Dhaga; it supplies no climate dataset or regional distribution. Distinct from existing Magha sayings.

odia: ଏ କଥାଟା ସତ, ହେଲେ ପାଉ ନାହିଁ
title: True, yet hard to believe
literal_meaning: This is true, yet it is not believed.
explanation: The line calls a statement true while registering a failure of belief. The headword’s second sense supplies that reading of the shortened ending. Our interpretation attends to the gap between asserting truth and finding something convincing; the line itself does not establish whether an unnamed statement is actually true.
meaning_odia: କଥାଟିକୁ ସତ ବୋଲି କହି ମଧ୍ୟ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେଉନଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଧରେ। ଶେଷର ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ବୁଝିବାରେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଅର୍ଥ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରେ। ଆମ ପାଠ ସତ ବୋଲି କହିବା ଓ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେବା ମଧ୍ୟର ଫରକକୁ ଦେଖେ। ଅଜଣା କଥାଟି ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ସତ କି ନୁହେଁ, ଏଥିରୁ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a claim of truth from the experience of believing it.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ସତ୍ୟର ଦାବିକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେବାର ଅନୁଭବଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ପାଠକ ଅପ୍ରତ୍ୟାଶିତ ହିସାବ ଦେଖି ପୁଣି ଗଣିଲେ। ସଂଖ୍ୟା କିପରି ଆସିଲା ବୁଝିବା ପରେ ସେ କଥାଟି ମାନିଲେ। / A reader checks an unexpected calculation and understands how its result was reached. This is an invented application, not evidence for the saying’s origin.
cultural_context: The quotation remains unfilled: it omits the headword’s ମନକୁ. Belief sense2, not approval sense1, supplies the literal rendering; no speaker identity or particular disputed fact is established.

odia: ପାଖରେ ଶୁଏ, କାନରେ କହେ, ତା କଥା କି ଅନାସ୍ଥା ହୁଏ
title: The nearby voice
literal_meaning: The one who sleeps nearby speaks into the ear—can their words be distrusted?
explanation: The question gives a nearby voice an apparent advantage. The dictionary places it under backbiting, making access to the listener part of the image. Our reading separates that closeness from reliability: being heard privately does not establish that a report is true. No spouse, gender or actual accusation is identified.
meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ସ୍ୱରକୁ ଏକ ସୁବିଧା ଦେଉଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଚୁଗୁଲି କହିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ନିକଟତାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱସନୀୟତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ—ଏକାନ୍ତରେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ବକ୍ତା ପତି ବା ପତ୍ନୀ, କେଉଁ ଲିଙ୍ଗର ବା କେଉଁ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading asks whether private access is being mistaken for trustworthy evidence.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, ଏକାନ୍ତରେ କହିବାର ସୁଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବି ନିଆଯାଉଛି କି।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ସଭା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ ସଦସ୍ୟ ଆଉଜଣଙ୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ଧୀର ସ୍ୱରରେ କିଛି କହିଲେ। ଶ୍ରୋତା ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ କଥା ମଧ୍ୟ ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / Before a meeting, a listener declines to judge another member from a private report alone. This scene is invented.
cultural_context: The earlier Krishna Singh Mahabharata Adi quotation illustrates whispering sense1. It is separate from this Dhaga under sense2 and does not establish its author.

odia: ଭାକୁଡ଼ମାଛ ଥାଇ ବୋଇଲା ମୁଁ ମାଛଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ରଜା ମୋ ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ସୋରୁଆ କଲେ ଦେଖିବୁ କେଡ଼େ ମଜା
title: The fish advertises its worth
literal_meaning: The bhakuda fish said: I am king among fish; make broth from my head and see how enjoyable it is.
explanation: The talking fish supports its royal claim with an offer of its own head for cooking. Our reading follows that odd self-advertisement: praise of its worth comes through what someone else might enjoy. This is a playful reading of the boast, not a supplied moral about sacrifice or a tested cooking recommendation.
meaning_odia: କଥା କହୁଥିବା ମାଛ ନିଜକୁ ରାଜା କହି ନିଜ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ରାନ୍ଧିବା କଥା ଆଗକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପାଠ ସେହି ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ ଆତ୍ମପ୍ରଶଂସାକୁ ଦେଖେ—ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଭଲ ଲାଗିବା ଭିତରେ ନିଜ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦର୍ଶାଯାଉଛି। ଏହା କଥାଟିର ରସମୟ ପାଠ; ଆତ୍ମତ୍ୟାଗର ଉପଦେଶ ବା ପରୀକ୍ଷିତ ରୋଷେଇ ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Our reading notices a boast that offers the speaker itself as evidence of its value.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆତ୍ମପ୍ରଶଂସାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବେ ବକ୍ତା ନିଜକୁ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣୁଛି।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ମାଛର ଗର୍ବିତ ସ୍ୱରରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପଢ଼ିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଦେଖିଲେ, ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ନିଜକୁ କେମିତି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣିଛି। / Readers perform the boast and discuss its peculiar offer. This reading-circle scene is invented, not a cooking demonstration.
cultural_context: The domestic noun gloss identifies bhakuda as Katla; earlier Sanskrit senses name Birata and Rohita separately. No species research, royal history, recipe or traditional sacrifice lesson is inferred.
